paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: words are small, but they steer a whole life. James says a tiny bit guides a horse and a very small rudder steers a ship (James 3:3-4). Then he says the tongue is the same, "a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things" (James 3:5). That's why he warns that teachers "will be judged more strictly" (James 3:1), because the more people hear you, the more your words carry.

Now here's the hard part, and I'm not going to dress it up. James says "no man can tame the tongue" (James 3:8). That means white-knuckling it, promising yourself to do better on Monday, won't fix it. I have stamped a lot of cookies crooked in my day, so I know what it is to say, "Never again," and then do it again. James opens with the same truth: "We all stumble in many ways" (James 3:2).

So what does he want from you? He wants you to see the problem when the same mouth blesses "our Lord and Father" and curses people "made in God's likeness" (James 3:9). Then he says, "My brothers, this should not be!" (James 3:10). A spring doesn't give both fresh water and salt water (James 3:11), so let your words match the One you praise. Ask God for help with it, and be careful what comes out of your mouth today.
